ACTION: Read the round-5 scoped re-review report for Task 5 in `.sdd/12-tide-cache/` to get the exact wording of F2.
ACTION: Read Task 5's brief in `.sdd/12-tide-cache/` to see what the Global Constraints and the task text say about a missing header line and about the interval.
ACTION: Read the header-parsing path in `tide/parse.py` to check that F2 is real in the current code.
ACTION: Edit the ledger. Append `Ruling: <decision> — <why> — <cost if wrong>` for F2 and close Task 5 at the cap. If F2 breaks a stated requirement, list it as load-bearing work for the final whole-branch review and for the plan-completion gate. I dispatch no sixth fix round.
ACTION: Run `scripts/task-brief` for Task 6 and dispatch its implementer with an explicit model, chosen per `references/model-selection.md`.

Task 5 has used all five fix attempts. Review finding F2 is still open: `tide/parse.py` accepts a negative interval when the header line is missing. The plan allows no more fix rounds, so I am now ruling on F2 myself.

I will stop and ask you only if the brief and the plan disagree about this case and any ruling would be a guess. Otherwise I record the ruling in the ledger and start Task 6.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- Rounds 1 to 3 resumed the same implementer, and rounds 4 and 5 used a fresh one. A resumed agent keeps its own failed attempts in context and can repeat them. A fresh agent does not.
- The five-attempt cap stops a loop that no longer converges. After the cap, the controller rules on the finding. It does not retry.
- A finding I rule as load-bearing is not dropped. It goes to the final whole-branch review and to the plan-completion gate, where you will see it in one batched question.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`
